subject: ela
skillName: Use technology to produce and publish writing
intro: These tasks ask you to make smart choices about producing and publishing writing with technology. Read each short task or message, then identify the best tool, feature, comment, or safe online choice.

items.prompt:
Read the task: 'You need to send a polite, formal request to your school principal asking permission to start a recycling club.' Which digital tool fits this purpose best?
Choose one: a group text to your friends, a formal email, a public blog post, a private journal app.

steps: The audience is one specific reader, the principal, and the tone needs to be formal and polite.
A group text and a public blog post reach the wrong audience, and a journal app is only for yourself.
A formal email reaches the principal directly and supports a respectful, formal tone, so it is the best choice.

items.prompt:
Read the goal: 'You want the three main sections of your report to stand out so readers can find them quickly.' Which word-processing feature best does this?
Choose one: change the font color of every word, add a heading to each section, make the whole document italic, make the page margins wider.
items.answer: Add a heading to each section.

steps: The goal is to help readers find and separate the main sections.
Changing every font color, making everything italic, or widening margins only changes appearance and does not label the sections.
Headings name and separate each section so readers can scan and jump to what they need, so this is the best feature.

items.prompt: Read the sentence in a draft: 'The principal of our school read the announcement.' Spell check shows no spelling errors, but one word might still be wrong for the meaning. Is this sentence using the correct word, and what does that tell you about spell check?
items.answer: Yes, 'principal' is correct here because it means the head of the school. This shows that spell check only checks spelling, so a writer must still read carefully to make sure each word fits the meaning.

steps: 'Principal' means the leader of a school, which is exactly what the sentence means, so the word is correct.
Spell check found no error because the word is spelled correctly.
The lesson is that spell check cannot tell whether a correctly spelled word is the right word, so the writer must reread to catch real-word errors.

items.prompt:
Read the comment a student left on a classmate's shared draft: 'This part is bad.' Which rewritten comment gives feedback that is specific, kind, and useful?
Choose one: 'I do not like it.', 'Great job, no changes.', 'Your second paragraph is clear, but the third one needs an example to support the point.', 'Why did you even write this?'
items.answer: 'Your second paragraph is clear, but the third one needs an example to support the point.'

steps: Helpful feedback points to a specific part, stays respectful, and suggests a clear improvement.
'I do not like it' and 'Why did you even write this?' are unkind and vague, and 'Great job, no changes' gives no useful direction.
The third comment names a specific paragraph and suggests adding an example, so it is specific, kind, and useful.

items.prompt:
Read the comment on your shared document: 'Could you add a source for this statistic?' Which is the best collaborative response?
Choose one: delete the comment without replying, reply 'Stop telling me what to do', reply 'Good point, I will add the link to the study', ignore it.
items.answer: Reply 'Good point, I will add the link to the study'.

steps: A good response to feedback accepts a useful suggestion and states a clear next step.
Deleting or ignoring the comment leaves the writing weaker, and 'Stop telling me what to do' is dismissive and unkind.
'Good point, I will add the link to the study' welcomes the feedback and explains what the writer will do, so it is the best response.

items.prompt:
Read the situation: 'You found a helpful fact for your report on a website.' What is the responsible way to use it?
Choose one: copy the sentences word for word with no mention of the site, put the fact in your own words and name the source, change a few words and claim it as your own, say a friend told you.
items.answer: Put the fact in your own words and name the source.

steps: Using someone else's words or ideas without credit is plagiarism.
Copying word for word, swapping a few words, or saying a friend told you all fail to give proper credit.
Putting the fact in your own words and naming the source credits the original site and avoids plagiarism, so it is the responsible choice.

items.prompt:
Read the scenario: 'You are about to publish your essay on the class blog.' Which choice shows safe, responsible online behavior?
Choose one: include your home address and phone number, use a respectful tone and leave out private personal details, post an unkind comment about a classmate, share a friend's password.
items.answer: Use a respectful tone and leave out private personal details.

steps: Safe online behavior means protecting personal information and respecting others.
Posting your home address and phone number, being unkind, or sharing a password are all unsafe or disrespectful.
Using a respectful tone and leaving out private details keeps you safe and treats others well, so it is the responsible choice.

items.prompt:
Read the goal: 'You want to type a three-page story in one sitting without your hands getting tired.' Which habit best supports steady, accurate keyboarding?
Choose one: look at the keys and type with one finger, rest your fingers on the home row and keep a steady rhythm, hit the keys as hard as possible, stop after every word to reread.
items.answer: Rest your fingers on the home row and keep a steady rhythm.

steps: Typing several pages in one sitting needs speed, accuracy, and stamina.
Hunting and pecking with one finger, hitting keys hard, or stopping after every word all slow you down or tire your hands.
Resting fingers on the home row and keeping a steady rhythm is touch typing, which builds the speed and stamina to type many pages, so it is the best habit.

items.prompt:
Read the task: 'Your group of four students all need to write and edit one report together at the same time.' Which digital tool fits this purpose best?
Choose one: a printed paper passed around, a shared online document, a private journal app, a one-way email blast.

steps: The purpose is for several people to write and edit the same report at the same time.
Printed paper can only be edited by one person at a time, a journal app is private, and a one-way email does not let the group edit together.
A shared online document lets everyone write, edit, and comment together, so it fits group work best.

items.prompt:
Read the goal: 'In your report you list five reasons in a row, and you want each reason to appear as its own separate item so it is easy to read.' Which word-processing feature best does this?
Choose one: a bulleted list, a larger font for the whole page, double spacing the whole document, a colorful background.

steps: The goal is to make each separate reason stand out as its own item.
A larger font, double spacing, or a colorful background change how the whole page looks but do not separate the reasons into items.
A bulleted list puts each reason on its own line with a bullet, making the list easy to read, so it is the best feature.

items.prompt: Read the sentence in a draft: 'I am going to bring my book over their.' Spell check shows no spelling errors, but one word is wrong for the meaning. Which word is wrong and what should it be?
items.answer: 'their' should be 'there', because 'there' refers to a place. Spell check did not catch it because 'their' is spelled correctly even though it is the wrong word.

steps: The sentence is about bringing a book to a place, so the correct word is 'there'.
'Their' shows ownership and does not fit this meaning.
Spell check accepted 'their' because it is spelled correctly, so the writer must catch this real-word error by rereading.

items.prompt: Read the comment on a classmate's shared draft: 'Your opening sentence really grabbed my attention. Could you add one detail to explain the second example?' Is this a helpful collaborative comment, and why?
items.answer: Yes, it is helpful because it is specific, kind, and useful. It names a part the writer did well, points to a specific spot (the second example), and suggests a clear improvement (adding one detail).

steps: Helpful feedback is specific, respectful, and gives a clear next step.
The comment praises a specific part, the opening sentence, in a kind tone.
It then points to the second example and suggests adding one detail, which is a concrete improvement, so the comment is helpful.

items.prompt:
Read the situation: 'You want to include a photo in your online report and let readers know what the photo shows.' Which word-processing feature best does this?
Choose one: insert the image and add a caption under it, change the font color, underline the title, widen the margins.
items.answer: Insert the image and add a caption under it.

steps: The goal is to add a photo and tell readers what it shows.
Changing font color, underlining the title, or widening margins do not add a photo or explain it.
Inserting the image and adding a caption shows the photo and labels what it shows, so it is the best feature.

items.prompt:
Read the scenario: 'A website you do not know asks you to type your full name, home address, and password to read an article for your report.' What is the safest choice?
Choose one: type all of the information so you can read it, do not share that private information and find the fact from a trusted source instead, share just your password, give a classmate's information.
items.answer: Do not share that private information and find the fact from a trusted source instead.

steps: Safe online behavior means protecting personal information such as your address and passwords.
Typing your private details, sharing your password, or giving a classmate's information all put personal information at risk.
Refusing to share the information and using a trusted source instead keeps you safe, so it is the best choice.

items.prompt:
Read the task: 'You want to publish your short story so that many readers, not just your teacher, can read it and leave comments.' Which digital tool fits this purpose best?
Choose one: a private journal app, a class blog or website post, a formal email to one person, a note saved only on your computer.
items.answer: A class blog or website post.

steps: The purpose is to publish writing so many readers can see it and comment.
A private journal, a note saved only on your computer, and an email to one person all reach only one person or no readers.
A class blog or website post publishes the story to many readers and lets them leave comments, so it fits the purpose best.
